assignment:
Some of your friends perform community service. For example, some tutor elementary school children and others clean up litter. They think helping the community is very important. But other friends of yours think community service takes too much time away from what they need or want to do. 
Your principal is deciding whether to require all students to perform community service. 
Write a letter to your principal in which you take a position on whether students should be required to perform community service. Support your position with examples.
essay_1:
Dear Principal Morales,

I heard that you are thinking about making every student do community service. I think you should do it. But it shouldn't be a ton of hours and we should get to pick what we do.

My first reason is that most kids are never going to try community service unless somebody makes them. Last spring my friend Dana started tutoring second graders at Lincoln Elementary. She only went because her older sister made her. She thought it was going to be so boring. Then she spent ten weeks helping a boy named Marcus sound out his words, and by May he was reading chapter books to her! Now Dana says she wants to be a teacher. She never would of known that if she didn't go, and I bet a lot of us are like that too.

My second reason is that it helps the town and you can see it with your own eyes. Some people in my neighborhood pick up trash on Creek Road one Saturday a month. Before they started, the ditch was full of bottles and fast food bags and it was gross. Now families go for walks there. Our school has around nine hundred students. If everybody did just twenty hours a year, that is eighteen thousand hours of tutoring and cleaning up and visiting nursing homes. Our town doesn't have the money to pay people for all that.

I know some kids are against this because my own friends told me. They have sports and jobs and little brothers and sisters to watch. They also have homework that keeps them up late already. I think that is fair, and it's why the rule has to be flexible. Twenty hours in a whole school year is only like half an hour a week. Kids should be allowed to finish in the summer if they want to. Also the school should count a lot of different things, like helping at a church food pantry or coaching little kids in soccer. If somebody babysits every day after school, they could do one weekend project and be done with it.

Some people also say that if you are forced to do it then it isn't real service. I don't agree with that. We are forced to take math, and nobody says the stuff we learn in math is fake. The rule just gets us in the door. After that it is up to us what we do with it.

I hope you will say yes to this and keep it flexible for us.

Sincerely,
An eighth grade student
essay_2:
Dear Principal Morales,

I am writing about the plan to make every student do community service. I think you should do it. The number of hours should be small, and there should be many ways to finish them.

My main reason is that most kids will not try service unless somebody makes them. Last spring my friend Dana signed up to tutor second graders at Lincoln Elementary. She didn't want to go. Her older sister took her there, and Dana told me it was going to be ten boring weeks. Then she got a boy named Marcus who could not sound out words. By May he was reading chapter books to her. Now Dana says she might become a teacher. She would not have found that out by herself, and I don't think the rest of us would either.

The town needs it too. Some people from my street pick up trash on Creek Road one Saturday a month. Before that the ditch was full of bottles and fast food bags, and nobody walked there. Now families do. Our school has about nine hundred students. If each one did twenty hours a year, that is eighteen thousand hours of tutoring, cleaning, and visiting nursing homes. Our town can't pay for those things, so right now much of it doesn't get done.

I know what kids will say, because my own friends complain about it. They have jobs, sports, little brothers and sisters to watch, and homework that keeps them up late. They are tired already. That is not a dumb worry, and it is why the rule can't be strict. Twenty hours in a school year is about half an hour a week. Students should be able to finish in the summer. The school should count many things, like working at a church food pantry or coaching little kids in soccer. A kid who babysits every afternoon could do one weekend project and be done.

Some people say forced service is not real service. I don't agree. We are forced to take math, and nobody says the math we learn is fake.

If the rule is too hard, kids will not like it, and some will cheat on their hours. If the rule is fair, I think most of us will do the hours, and a few will keep going after they finish, the way Dana did. Please think about that when you write the rule.

Sincerely,
An eighth grade student
